attribution.note: Marcus's own words, in his own hot-take bullet on his Substack post.

semantics.note: The sentence frames this as the lesson DeepSeek has already shown, so reading it as an observation about demonstrated efficiency gains is faithful. 'Can' states what is achievable; it is not a probabilistic hedge. The speculation about dozens of GPUs that follows uses 'might' and is correctly left out.

contract.note: Marcus gave no metric. The plain reading (large, multiple-fold cuts in compute for broadly comparable capability) is ordinary and is not stretched either way. Excluding the dozens-of-GPUs speculation is fair. The inferred reporting window fits the post's context.

evidence.note: DeepSeek's own technical report, dated before the post: 2.788M H800 GPU hours for full V3 training, with performance comparable to leading models. This is a company disclosure, and it excludes earlier research runs.

Independent Epoch analysis, dated 2025-01-17, inside the window. It estimates about ten times less training compute than the similarly performing Llama 3.1 405B. It is an estimate built on the reported hours and an assumed hardware utilisation.
METR evaluation published after the window. V3 trails some models on RE-Bench. That limits claims of full capability parity but does not remove the large training-compute savings.

reviews.rationale: DeepSeek's report (e1) and an independent estimate (e2) together show roughly a tenfold cut in training compute against a model of similar benchmark performance. That counts as 'vast' on the plain reading. The resource figures are company-reported, and METR's later results (e3) limit claims of parity on every task. Neither point erases the large demonstrated gain, so the contract's support condition is met.
